question.problem:
Rationalize the denominator of the following expression:
$\sqrt{\frac{11}{pq}}\,=\,$ {{field-1}}
$pq$
question.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{11}{pq}} & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{pq}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to remove the radical $\sqrt{pq}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{pq},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{pq}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{pq}}{\sqrt{pq}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{11pq}}{(\sqrt{pq})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{11pq}}{pq}\end{aligned}
$$
